answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token in a public registry before it may submit jobs, with the lock held until its work is audited and any proven fraud triggers slashing. One person can still create many identities, but each nebula of sockpuppets now needs separate capital, and the attacker risks losing it; rotating names or making them wander across accounts does not restore slashed stake. A cipher-based signature can bind each job to its registered key, preventing cheap impersonation of another agent.
